This case is arising out of other than Police report, the private complaint filed by the Mr.B.V.Dikshit Kumar S/o Late.B.S.Venkataratham against the accused for the alleged C.C.No.31304/2018 offences punishable under section 406 and 420 of Indian Penal Code.

2. It is the case of the complainant that the accused acquainted with him, he borrowed an amount of Rs.8 lakhs with promise to return the said amount within 10 days, but the accused did not repay the said amount.

When the complainant repeatedly requests the accused to return the borrowed amount, the accused had issued cheques bearing No.811100 for Rs.4,24,000/ and another cheque for Rs.4,24,000/ dated 16.06.2010 respectively.
The complainant as per the direction of the accused presented the said cheques for clearance, the said cheques were dishonoured.

Thereafter,
the complainant issued notice to the accused, even after issuance of notice to the accused, he has not repaid the amount.
Hence, the complainant has filed complaint against the accused under section 138 of Negotiable Instruments Act.

During the adjudication of case of Negotiable Instruments Act it learnt to the complainant that the accused has fraudulently and deliberately issued cheques belongs to his mother as if belongs to his cheque with an intention to cheat and defraud the C.C.No.31304/2018 complainant.
On the said ground only Hon'ble XX ACMM, Court, Bengaluru acquitted the accused.

Therefore, the complainant filed this private complaint against the accused for the offences punishable under section 406 and 420 of IPC as the accused intentionally to cheat the complainant issued his mother cheque as if his cheque and thereby he has committed offences punishable under section 406 and 420 of IPC.
3.
Initially the complainant has filed this private complaint against the present accused Sri.M.Kemparaju and his wife.

Against the wife of accused i.e., accused No.2, it is alleged that she B.V.Dikshit Kumar vs M.Kemparaju on 16 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/138614203/
2 was issued cheque even after closing of her account with an intention to cheat the complainant.

report.
In service of process the accused appeared before the court and enlarged on bail.

4. The prosecution papers supplied to the accused thereafter recording of evidence before the charge of complainant, having heard both side framed charge for the offences punishable under section 406 and 420 of IPC and read over and explained to the accused.
The accused pleaded not guilty and claimed to be tried.
5. The complainant in order to prove his case examined himself as PW1 and got marked Exs.P1 to 14 documents and examined one witness as PW2 and closed his side.
6. Incriminating circumstance has appeared against the accused in the prosecution evidence read over and explained to him.
Having understood the same the accused has given his statement under section 313 of Cr.PC and same has been duly recorded by this court.
The accused did not C.C.No.31304/2018 choose to lead defence evidence.
But confronting to the PW1 in cross examination got marked Exs.D1 to D5 documents.

7. Heard arguments on both side.
8.
The following points arise for court's consideration, POINTS 1.

Whether the prosecution beyond reasonable doubts proves that, the accused borrowed Rs.8 lakhs from the complainant and issued cheque of his mother as his cheque on 16.06.2010 and thereby committed criminal breach of trust thereby committed an offences punishable under section 406 of IPC.
2.

Whether the prosecution, beyond reasonable doubt, proves that the accused with an intention to cheat the complainant dishonestly inducing the complainant deceived to deliver of an amount of Rs.8 lakhs and issued cheque of his mother as his cheque bearing No.811100 dated 16.06.2010 and C.C.No.31304/2018 thereby committed an offence punishable under section 420 of IPC.
3. What order?
9. The court's answer to the above points is as follows;
Point No.1 : In the Negative.
Point No.2 : In the Affirmative.

REASONS 10. Point No.1 and 2:
It is the specific case of the complainant that the accused who is his friend borrowed loan of Rs.8 lakhs to meet his financial commitments and domestic needs on 06.02.2010.
The accused promised to repay the same within 10 days.
But the accused failed to repay the said amount within 10 days.
The accused executed on Demand Promissory Note on 06.02.2010 for Rs.4 lakhs each.

When the complainant repeatedly demands to repay the amount accused issued two cheques one of his cheque and another one was his wife's cheque for Rs.4,24,000/ each on 16.06.2010 bearing No.831100 and 896895 respectively.
As per the advice of the C.C.No.31304/2018 accused when the complainant presented the said cheques for collection, the said cheques were dishonoured.
The said cheques were returned as "Account Closed".
Thereafter the complainant issued legal notice to the accused and his wife.
The said notice was served upon the accused and his wife.
The accused replied to the notice of complainant by denying the transaction.
Thereafter, the complainant filed case against the accused person for the offence punishable U/s.138 of Negotiable Instruments Act in CC.No.49909/2010.
During the trial it came to know that the accused with an intention to cheat the complainant issued cheque of his mother as his cheque.
On the said reason only the accused acquitted in the said case.
In the said case even though the accused issued the cheque in question by signing the cheque.
But the dishonour of the said cheque not come under the purview of Section 138 of N.I.Act.
Hence the Court acquitted him.
Intention of accused clearly reveals that intentionally to cheat the complainant issued his mother's cheque as his cheque.

Hence, the accused committed an offence punishable U/s.406 and 420 of IPC.
C.C.No.31304/2018 11.
On the other hand, the accused has taken the defence that he never borrowed loan of Rs.8 lakhs from the complainant.
The complainant was running chits business, he (accused) invested in the chits funds of complainant.
At that time he issued two cheques for the purpose of security, the complainant misused the said cheques and filed false cases.
Hence prayed to acquitted him.
12. The complainant in order to prove his case, examined himself as PW1 wherein he deposed par with complainant and he relied on Ex.P.1 to P.14 documents.
Ex.P.1 is the certified copy of Judgment in CC.No.49909/2010, which discloses that the present complainant filed case for the offence punishable U/s.138 of N.I.Act against the present accused.

In the said case the accused had taken the defence that the cheque in question was not belongs to his account and signature on the cheque was also not scribed him and he denied the loan transaction with the complainant and also denied the execution of promissory note.
In support of his defence, accused examined Chief Manager of State Bank of Hyderabad as DW2.

In the said case the DW2 deposed that C.C.No.31304/2018 Ex.P.1 cheque was belongs to old account No.01190013284 and New account No.52116726865 which belongs to one Kallamma W/o.T.Mariyappa who is the mother of the accused.
The said Manager also produced account opening form in the said case which was marked as Ex.D.6.
The said Kallamma used to put thumb impression and she did not known to sign.

Therefore, the Hon'ble XX ACMM Court Bengaluru come to the conclusion that the issuance of B.V.Dikshit Kumar vs M.Kemparaju on 16 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/138614203/
4 cheque is not belongs to the account of the accused and dishonour of the said cheque not attracted the offence of 138 of N.I.Act.

Ex.P.3 is the Certified copy of of Return memo dated 18 th June 2010 which clearly reveals that the said cheque returned as "Funds Insufficient".

14. It is relevant to note here that the question arises whether the money transaction between the complainant and accused and issuance of cheque of 3rd person as each cheque by the accused is attracted section 406 of IPC.
The complainant has to establish the following ingredients.
15. In order to prove Section 406 of IPC the prosecution has to prove ingredients explained in Section 405 of IPC.

The ingredients in order to constitute a criminal breach of trust are:(i) entrusting a person with property or with any dominion over property,
(ii) that person entrusted (a) dishonestly misappropriating or converting that property to C.C.No.31304/2018 his own use; or (b) dishonestly using or disposing of that property or willfully suffering any other person so to do in violation (i) of any direction of law prescribing the mode in which such trust is to be discharged, (ii) of any legal contract made, touching the discharge of such trust.
16.

In view of the above provision it clears that to attract section 406 of IPC i.e., criminal breach of trust would, interalia meaning using or disposing of her property by person who is entrusted that or otherwise as dominion.
Such an act means not only dishonestly, but also in violation of any direction of law or any contract express or implied relating to carrying out trust.
However, in the instant case, materials on record failed to satisfy the ingredients of Section 405 of IPC.

In the absence of evidence establish entrustment, dishonest misappropriation, conversion, use or disposal,
which action should be in violation of any direction of law or legal contract.

The learned advocate for complainant argued that the accused dishonestly issued his mother's cheque as his cheque by putting his signature thereby committed an offence C.C.No.31304/2018 punishable under section 406 of IPC.
No doubt, the accused issued his mother's cheque as his cheque with dishonest intention but it is not attract section 406 of IPC.
There is no entrustment or misappropriation.

sentences.text: In order to comply Section 420 of IPC, namely cheating and dishonestly inducing delivery of property, ingredients of Section 415 of IPC have to be satisfied.

To constitute an offence of cheating under section 415 of IPC, a person should be induced, either in fraudulently or dishonestly, to delivery any property to any person, or concerned that any person shall retain any property.

Thus,
the sign quo non of Section 415 of IPC is "Fraudulent", "Dishonestly", or "Intentionally Inducement", and absence of these elements would debase the offence of cheating.

In the present case on hand the complainant specifically contended that the accused borrowed the loan by assuring to repay the same within 10 days by executing On Demand Promissory Note of Rs.4 lakh each as per Ex.P12 and 13 respectively.
The accused denied the said contention and contended that he had invested in chits fund with complainant and issued C.C.No.31304/2018 two cheques for the purpose of security.
In this regard the accused has not produced any documents.
On the other hand the complainant produced Ex.P12 and 13.
Ex. P12
and 13
are the Pronotes executed by accused person.
The accused has not specifically denied these documents.

It is relevant to note here that when the said cheques returned as account closed this complainant initiated the case against the accused for the offence punishable under section 138 of Negotiable Instruments Act, after due following process of law in CC No.49909/2010.
Wherein this accused had taken defence that the cheque in question was not belongs to him and signature was not belongs to him and
in order to prove his defence examined Manager of the Bank as DW2.

The DW2 in the said case deposed that the said cheque in question was belongs to mother of accused and said mother of accused by name Kallamma W/o Mariyappa did not know to sign, she used to put thumb impression.
On careful perusal of Ex.P2 there is signature of accused was appeared.
The accused merely denied the said signature if he would have not put the said signature he would have filed application for expert's C.C.No.31304/2018 opinion.
But he did not to do so.
The complainant also not claimed expert's opinion.
Neither the complainant nor the accused have not taken the assistance of handwriting experts to prove their respective contention.
Hence, the court left with no other option except to look for the comparision of admitted signature of accused with disputed signature as per Section 73 of Indian Evidence Act.

Section 73 of Indian Evidence Act, empowers the court to compare the signature, writing etc., in ordinary course the courts did not make any venture to exercise the power conferred under section 73 of Evidence Act.
But in the present case neither the complainant nor the accused taken steps to refer the signatures to the hand writing experts.
Therefore, in this background this court compare the admitted signature with the disputed signatures with bare eyes.
The signature appeared on the 313 statement, charge and vakalath nama of accused is treated as admitted signatures.
The signature appeared on the Ex.P2 certified copy of cheque is treated as disputed signature.

On comparing the signatures of accused on statement of accused under section 313 of Cr.PC, charge and vakalath along with C.C.No.31304/2018 disputed signature i.e., Ex.P2, it appears no variations of signatures appeared on vakalath, statement of accused under section 313 and charge and Ex.P2.
In all these signatures are belongs to accused.
There is informity in all signatures, all signatures are same and there is no changes in the signatures.
Therefore, the signature of accused on the Ex.P2 and admitted signatures are resembled similar.
18. As per Ex.P1 and Ex.D5 which are one and the same.
Admittedly the accused issued the cheque as per Ex.P 2 to the complainant.
He contended that he issued the said cheque along with cheque of his wife for purpose of security regarding chit fund business but no documents has been placed.

As per the Ex.P12 and 13 clearly reveals that the accused had borrowed the hand loan of B.V.Dikshit Kumar vs M.Kemparaju on 16 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/138614203/
6 Rs.8 lakhs by executing pro notes and when complainant demanded to repaying of loan the accused intentionally issued his mother's cheque as his cheque by putting his signature on the Ex.P2 cheque.
It clearly goes to show that his intention.
The accused dishonestly and fraudulently to inducing the amount issued his mother's cheque as his cheque.
It clearly shows his C.C.No.31304/2018 dishonest and intentionally inducement.

When the complainant filed criminal case for the offence punishable under section 138 Negotiable Instruments Act, in CC No.49909/2010, accused himself admitted that the cheque was belongs to his mother.
It clearly shows his intention to dupe the amount received from complainant issued his mother's cheque as his cheque.
Therefore, section 420 is attracted to the case on hand, the accused committed an offence punishable under section 420 of IPC.
On careful reading of entire evidence of complainant and perusal of materials placed by complainant, it clearly attracted section 420 of IPC.
Hence, on the evidence of complainant and documentary evidence it is sufficient to believe the case of the prosecution.
Hence, the complainant has proved the guilt of the accused beyond all reasonable doubt for the offence punishable under section 420 of IPC.
But he failed to prove the allegations against the accused for the offence punishable under section 406 of IPC.
Therefore, this court has answered Point No.1 in the Negative and Point No.2 in the Affirmative.
In the result, I proceed to pass the following:

::ORDER::
In exercising the powers conferred under Section 248(2) of the Cr.P.C., the accused is found guilty for the offences punishable under Section 420 of IPC.
In exercising the powers conferred under Section 248(1) of the Cr.P.C., the accused is hereby acquitted for the offences punishable under Section 406 of IPC.
For hearing on sentence.
